text:
support_jen: FYI customer 'AcmeMaps' opened a high-sev ticket — p99 latency in eu-west has jumped from ~200ms to 5-7s since 09:12 UTC. Several user complaints. Request IDs attached in ticket.
oncall_mike: Acknowledged. Can you paste a couple of the request ids + which model they were hitting? Also are errors timeouts or backend 500s?
support_jen: Two sample ids: req_9a7f, req_b3c2. Model = redwood/gpt-3-large-v1 (hosted). No 500s in ticket, just very slow token streaming and some client timeouts.
oncall_mike: Ping infra_sara and kevin. I'm going to start triage steps. @infra_sara @kevin (eng-runtime)
infra_sara: Looking at cluster metrics now. eu-west GPU pool showing CPU pressure on routing plane + an uptick in queue depth at the ingest layer around 09:10–09:20 UTC.
kevin (eng-runtime): I see increased KV cache churn and higher tail latencies on long contexts. Could be a batch sizing/sequence-length mix causing slow kernels. Also seeing a spike of large seq requests from a single API key.
devon (network): No network-wide packet loss. Egress to eu-west looks fine. No infra maintenance.
oncall_mike: Immediate mitigations we can do in parallel:
- throttle the offending API key (reduce QPS) — support can action a soft rate limit.
- set circuit breaker on high-p99 paths (fail fast after 2s) so clients get quick 503s instead of long streaming delays.
- enable fallback routing for new requests from eu-west -> serve from us-west if model variant present.
- temporarily force a lower-latency model variant (gpt-3-small-v1) for the customer's requests.
support_jen: Acting on throttle now — applying temporary 10 rps cap and notifying the customer.
oncall-bot: [action] rate-limit applied to api-key:acmemaps (10 RPS) by support_jen at 09:26 UTC
infra_sara: Starting to flip circuit breaker config for route /v1/generate. Will add a p99 cutoff at 2s and a 10s open window. Patch below:
```
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "cb": { "threshold_ms": 2000, "open_for_s": 10, "max_consecutive_failures": 5 }
}
```
kevin (eng-runtime): Pushing a quick routing policy override: for api-key:acmemaps set fallback_region:us-west and model_alias:fast-quantized. Command:
```
POST /admin/override
{
  "api_key": "acmemaps",
  "fallback_region": "us-west",
  "model_alias": "gpt-3-large-v1-quant-fast"
}
```
oncall-bot: [info] routing override enqueued. Expected propagation ~30s.
oncall_mike: Also enabling aggressive prefix caching for common prompts from that key to avoid regen work. If anyone can run a quick query on top prompt patterns that'd help.
kevin (eng-runtime): Cache rules applied. Observed that 42% of requests from that key share the same 1st 128 tokens pattern.
support_jen: Customer notified of temporary throttling and failover. They asked if we can roll back if it degrades UX.
oncall_mike: Yes — these are reversible. Plan timeline:
1) immediate throttling + circuit breaker + routing override (done/in-progress)
2) monitor p95/p99 for 15 minutes
3) if stable, gradually relax throttle and remove routing override
4) if not stable, consider rolling model version back (previous stable commit) for eu-west
infra_sara: Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.net/d/latency/eu-west-p99 (watch p95/p99, queue depth, and dispatch rate). I'm seeing p99 drop from 6.8s -> 1.9s after the CB flip + routing override starting to propagate.
kevin (eng-runtime): Good sign. Also adding a temporary batching cap to avoid huge batches forming: set max_batch_tokens=2048 for the affected worker pool.
devon (network): Route weights updated; new requests are flowing to us-west fallback. No cross-region errors seen.
support_jen: Customer reports immediate improvement for some users, others still see delays — they're okay with staged rollback once metrics look good.
oncall_mike: Evidence collection: please attach the following to the ticket:
- two full traces for req_9a7f, req_b3c2 (from tracing service)
- stack traces from the routing plane for 09:08–09:30
- GPU utilization and queue depth screenshots
- the admin override audit log
kevin (eng-runtime): Collected traces and uploaded to ticket: https://tickets.redwood.com/ACME-438/trace-uploads
infra_sara: I'll keep an eye for regression after we relax throttle. Set an alert: if p99 > 2s for 5m, auto-reopen this thread and escalate to eng-runtime.
oncall-bot: [alert rule set] p99_alert_eu_west >2s for 5m -> notify #eng-oncall
oncall_mike: Postmortem notes / quick mitigation playbook (short):
- detect: p95/p99 spike in region
- immediate: soft throttle offending api_key, enable circuit breaker (2s p99), route to fallback region/model, enable prefix cache
- intermediate: reduce max_batch_tokens, apply faster quantized model alias
- long-term: add per-key sequence-length quotas, improve kernel selection heuristics for high-seq tails
support_jen: Customer closed loop: they said UX acceptable now and will escalate if see any regressions. Marking as monitored.
kevin (eng-runtime): Follow-up: we'll run a small A/B to see if kernel selection change fixes tail without fallback. Scheduling for next maintenance window.
oncall_mike: Thanks team. If p99 stays <2s for 30m we'll remove emergency overrides. Leaving thread open for alerts. :thumbsup:
